nomenclature.etymology_html:
-Flueggea : In memory of the German physician and botanist Johann Flugge (1775-1816).
-Leucopyrus : From the Greek leuco "white" and pyrus "pear", in reference of the white-coloured fruit of the plant.

stem_bark.text: The bark of Flueggea leucopyrus is greyish-coloured, rough and longitudinally fissured.
stem_bark.text_html: The bark of Flueggea leucopyrus is greyish-coloured, rough and longitudinally fissured.

seed.text: The seeds of Flueggea leucopyrus are crescent-shaped, 2.5 mm long and 1.5 mm wide. The seed is light brown-coloured and there are 3-4 seeds per fruit.
seed.text_html: The seeds of Flueggea leucopyrus are crescent-shaped, 2.5 mm long and 1.5 mm wide. The seed is light brown-coloured and there are 3-4 seeds per fruit.

fruit.text: The fruit of Flueggea leucopyrus is a subglobose berry. The fruit is 5 mm across, green turning white when ripe.
fruit.text_html: The fruit of Flueggea leucopyrus is a subglobose berry. The fruit is 5 mm across, green turning white when ripe.

flower.text: The flowers of Flueggea leucopyrus are grouped in axillary clusters (few-flowered cymes). The flowers of Flueggea leucopyrus are unisexual (male and female flowers separated on the same individual). The male flowers have a 3-4 mm pedicel and 5 tepals . The tepals are ovate, 1 cm long and 0.7 cm wide and yellowish-coloured. The androecium is composed of 5 stamens. The filaments are 1.5 cm with small and globose anthers. The female flowers have 5 ovate and 0.8 mm long tepals . The styles are 0.7 mm long, connate at the base and with bifid stigmas. The ovary is ovoid, 0.5 cm across and 2-3-celled. The flowers are fragrant.
flower.text_html:
The flowers of Flueggea leucopyrus are grouped in axillary clusters (few-flowered cymes).
The flowers of Flueggea leucopyrus are unisexual (male and female flowers separated on the same individual).
The male flowers have a 3-4 mm pedicel and 5 tepals. The tepals are ovate, 1 cm long and 0.7 cm wide and yellowish-coloured.
The androecium is composed of 5 stamens. The filaments are 1.5 cm with small and globose anthers.
The female flowers have 5 ovate and 0.8 mm long tepals.
The styles are 0.7 mm long, connate at the base and with bifid stigmas. The ovary is ovoid, 0.5 cm across and 2-3-celled.
The flowers are fragrant.

leaf.text: The leaves of Flueggea leucopyrus grow alternately on the stem (spirally arranged). The leaf is simple, bright green-coloured above and paler beneath. The leaf is coriaceous and glabrous on both sides. The leaves have a 5 mm long petiole . The leaf of Flueggea leucopyrus is 2-4 cm long and 1.5-3 cm wide. The shape of the blade is obovate, the apex is rounded, the base is cuneate and the margins are entire. The venation of the leaf is reticulate with a prominent midrib.
leaf.text_html:
The leaves of Flueggea leucopyrus grow alternately on the stem (spirally arranged).
The leaf is simple, bright green-coloured above and paler beneath. The leaf is coriaceous and glabrous on both sides.
The leaves have a 5 mm long petiole.
The leaf of Flueggea leucopyrus is 2-4 cm long and 1.5-3 cm wide. The shape of the blade is obovate, the apex is rounded, the base is cuneate and the margins are entire.
The venation of the leaf is reticulate with a prominent midrib.

habit.text: Flueggea leucopyrus is a thorny and deciduous shrub growing up to 4-5 m high. It is profusely branched and it has arrested (thorn-like) and stiff branchlets.
habit.text_html: Flueggea leucopyrus is a thorny and deciduous shrub growing up to 4-5 m high. It is profusely branched and it has arrested (thorn-like) and stiff branchlets.

reproduction_dispersal.text: Flueggea leucopyrus is monoecious with unisexual (male or female) flowers on the same individual. Flueggea leucopyrus is pollinated by a wide variety of insects (mainly by honey bees). The seeds of Flueggea leucopyrus are mainly dispersed by frugivorous birds and mammals.
reproduction_dispersal.text_html:
• Sex distribution :

    Flueggea leucopyrus is monoecious with unisexual (male or female) flowers on the same individual.

  • Mode of pollination :

    Flueggea leucopyrus is pollinated by a wide variety of insects (mainly by honey bees).

  • Seed dispersal :

    The seeds of Flueggea leucopyrus are mainly dispersed by frugivorous birds and mammals.

reforestation.text: Flueggea leucopyrus is able to flourish in a wide range of soils but all soils need to be free draining. It thrives in open areas (it prefers full sunlight). The species is propagated by seeds. 12 hours of soaking in water accelerates the germination process.
reforestation.text_html:
• Planting advice and requirements :

    Flueggea leucopyrus is able to flourish in a wide range of soils but all soils need to be free draining. It thrives in open areas (it prefers full sunlight).
    The species is propagated by seeds.

  • Seed treatments :

    12 hours of soaking in water accelerates the germination process.
